meta.title: ᱫᱩᱨᱜᱚ Mantra — 108 Japa | Japam
meta.description: ᱫᱩᱨᱜᱚ mantra meaning, 108 japa steps, and practice in Japam.

runs.text: Durga bhakti includes steady mantra japa as a foundation of daily practice.
Japam uses the mantra below during match-3 play with counting toward 108.
Chant with a calm mind, offering salutation rather than demanding specific outcomes.

items: Builds daily discipline and mental focus
Complements temple puja — does not replace it
Sit in a quiet place with spine straight
Chant 108 times on a mala (one round)
Keep attention on the mantra sound and meaning
Close with gratitude to your ishta devata

runs.text: Any sincere daily time works; ask your priest for festival or vrat days specific to this deity.
Select Durga in Japam to hear the mantra audio and track your japa count.

faqs.question: How many times should I chant Durga's mantra?
faqs.answer: 108 repetitions (one mala) is the common standard; some do 11 or 21 malas under guidance.

faqs.question: Can I use Japam without signing in?
faqs.answer: Guest try mode is available from the landing page; sign in to save long-term progress.

faqs.question: Is this the only mantra for this deity?
faqs.answer: Your lineage may use stotras or longer mantras; this is the form in the Japam app.

faqs.question: Does mantra japa replace puja?
faqs.answer: No — japa supports home practice; formal puja follows your sampradaya.

faqs.question: Which direction should I face?
faqs.answer: East or north is common; consistency matters more than perfect direction.
